subjects.title: Maths
subjects.framework: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

units.title: Rational and irrational numbers
goals: Tell rational numbers from irrational ones
Estimate irrational numbers like √2 on a number line

units.title: Exponent rules
goals: Use the rules of integer exponents, like adding exponents when multiplying powers of the same number

units.title: Square and cube roots
goals: Solve x² = p and x³ = p with square and cube roots

units.title: Scientific notation
goals: Write very big and very small numbers in scientific notation and compute with them

units.title: Slope and proportional relationships
goals: Graph proportional relationships and read the unit rate as the slope
Explain y = mx + b

units.title: Linear equations
goals: Solve equations with the unknown on both sides
Tell when an equation has one, no or many solutions

units.title: Systems of equations
goals: Solve two equations together by graphing, substitution and elimination

units.title: Functions
goals: Explain that a function gives exactly one output for each input
Tell linear from non-linear functions

units.title: Linear models
goals: Build a function for a straight-line relationship and read its rate and its start
Describe graphs in words

units.title: Expanding and factorising
standards: SG S2 algebraic expressions, quadratic functions
goals: Expand brackets such as (a + b)² and (a + b)(a − b)
Factorise simple quadratic expressions
See the U-shape of y = x²

units.title: Transformations
goals: Describe rotations, reflections, translations and dilations with coordinates

units.title: Congruence and similarity
goals: Tell congruent and similar shapes by a sequence of transformations

units.title: Angles in triangles and parallel lines
goals: Use the angle sum of a triangle and the angles made by parallel lines and a transversal

units.title: The Pythagorean theorem
goals: Explain the Pythagorean theorem and use it to find lengths and distances

units.title: Sine, cosine and tangent
standards: UK KS3 (trigonometric ratios in right-angled triangles)
goals: Name the sides of a right-angled triangle
Use sin, cos and tan to find a side or an angle

units.title: Volume of cylinders, cones and spheres
goals: Use the volume formulas for cylinders, cones and spheres

units.title: Scatter plots and lines of fit
goals: Make scatter plots and describe their patterns
Fit a line and use it to predict

units.title: Two-way tables
goals: Read and make two-way tables to find patterns of association

units.title: Forces and motion
goals: Use Newton's third law for things that collide
Explain how forces change motion and how mass matters

units.title: Pressure
goals: Explain pressure in solids, liquids and gases
Explain floating and sinking

units.title: Kinetic and potential energy
goals: Relate kinetic energy to mass and speed
Explain how potential energy changes with distance

units.title: Energy, power and bills
standards: UK KS3 (energy: power ratings, domestic bills)
goals: Explain power in watts
Work out the cost of energy at home
Find ways to save it

units.title: Hot and cold reactions
goals: Tell exothermic from endothermic changes
Explain uses such as hand warmers and cold packs

units.title: Current, voltage and resistance
goals: Measure current and voltage
Compare series and parallel circuits
Explain resistance

units.title: Electricity and magnetism
goals: Describe what makes electric and magnetic forces stronger
Show that fields act at a distance

units.title: Waves
goals: Describe waves by amplitude and wavelength
Explain how waves are reflected, absorbed or passed through materials

units.title: Digital signals
goals: Explain why digital signals send information more reliably than analogue ones

units.title: Gravity and orbits
goals: Explain that gravity pulls every mass towards every other and keeps planets and moons in orbit
Compare gravity on the Moon and the planets

units.title: The solar system
goals: Compare the sizes, distances and features of the planets and moons

units.title: Moon phases, eclipses and seasons
goals: Model the Sun, Earth and Moon to explain Moon phases, eclipses and seasons

units.title: Transport in plants and animals
goals: Explain how water and food move in plants (xylem, phloem)
Explain how the heart, blood and lungs work together

units.title: Genes and heredity
goals: Explain how genes pass from parents to young and why young differ

units.title: Breeding and genes
goals: Explain selective breeding
Describe genetic engineering and the questions it raises

units.title: Natural selection
goals: Explain how helpful traits become more common in a population over generations

units.title: The fossil record
goals: Use fossils and body structures to find patterns in the history of life

units.title: The strongest evidence
goals: Choose the evidence that most strongly supports what you say about a text

units.title: Dialogue and incidents
goals: Explain how lines of dialogue or incidents move a story, show characters or lead to decisions

units.title: Point of view and dramatic irony
goals: Explain how a reader knowing more than a character creates suspense or humour

units.title: Old stories, new versions
goals: Explain how modern stories draw on myths, traditional tales and older works

units.title: Comparing texts
goals: Compare how two texts are built
Find where two texts disagree about facts

units.title: Central ideas and how they develop
goals: Follow how a central idea develops through supporting ideas

units.title: Evaluating arguments
goals: Find evidence in an argument that does not belong

units.title: Gerunds, participles and infinitives
goals: Explain what verbals do in a sentence

units.title: Active and passive voice
goals: Use active and passive voice for effect

units.title: Verb moods
goals: Use the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional and subjunctive moods

units.title: Ellipses and dashes
goals: Use commas, ellipses and dashes for a pause or a break

units.title: Irony and puns
goals: Explain verbal irony and puns

units.title: Word relationships and connotation
goals: Use relationships between words and their connotations

units.title: Finding good sources
goals: Judge which sources can be trusted and quote them correctly

units.title: Argue like a pro
goals: Tell claims from counterclaims
Use trustworthy sources
Write a strong conclusion

units.title: Explain complex ideas
goals: Organise complex information with headings, graphics and precise words

units.title: Craft a narrative
goals: Use flashback, reflection and telling details

units.title: Present with multimedia
goals: Present findings clearly with evidence and well-chosen media

subjects.title: History
subjects.framework: England's National Curriculum (KS2-KS3) with California world history, Cambridge Humanities and C3

units.title: The Industrial Revolution
goals: Describe steam, factories and railways
Explain how work and towns changed

units.title: Ideas of liberty
standards: UK KS3 (the Enlightenment, American independence, the French revolutionary wars)
goals: Explain Enlightenment ideas about rights
Describe the American and French revolutions and what they claimed
units.hard: the Terror and the revolutionary wars

units.title: Slavery and abolition
standards: UK KS3 (the transatlantic slave trade: its effects and its eventual abolition)
goals: Explain the transatlantic slave trade truthfully and with care
Describe the people who resisted and campaigned to end it
units.hard: the transatlantic slave trade and enslavement

units.title: Empires and independence
standards: UK KS3 (Indian independence and the end of Empire)
goals: Explain how empires grew
Describe how countries such as India won independence
units.hard: empire, the Bengal famine and the violence of partition

units.title: Votes for all
goals: Describe the campaign for women's votes and the growth of voting rights

units.title: The First World War
goals: Explain why it began
Describe life on the home front
Explain why we remember
units.hard: the First World War's battles and deaths

units.title: The Second World War
goals: Explain its causes
Describe evacuation and the home front
Explain how it ended and why we remember
units.hard: the Second World War, the Blitz, Hiroshima and Nagasaki

units.title: The Holocaust: remembering
goals: Explain how prejudice grew into the persecution and murder of Europe's Jews and others
Remember the victims and the rescuers
Explain why we remember
units.hard: the Holocaust: persecution and murder of Europe's Jews

units.title: Building peace and rights
standards: UK KS3 (Britain's place in the world since 1945)
goals: Describe the United Nations and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
Describe civil rights movements
units.hard: segregation, apartheid and the struggle for civil rights

units.title: From the space race to the digital age
goals: Describe the Moon landing, computers and the internet
Explain how technology changed daily life

subjects.title: Geography
subjects.framework: England's National Curriculum (KS2-KS3) with Cambridge Humanities and C3

units.title: Climate change
goals: Describe the evidence, causes and effects
Describe what people are doing about it

units.title: Development
goals: Measure development (life expectancy, schooling, income)
Explain why it differs

units.title: A connected world
goals: Explain globalisation through trade, travel and communication

units.title: Energy for the world
goals: Compare fossil fuels and renewables
Explain where energy comes from

units.title: Feeding the world
goals: Compare farming systems
Explain food miles and water for farming

units.title: Cities of the future
goals: Explain the challenges of megacities: transport, housing, green spaces

units.title: Tourism
goals: Weigh the good and bad effects of tourism
Explain sustainable tourism

units.title: Oceans and seas
goals: Explain currents and marine life
Describe the problem of plastic

units.title: Maps of the world
goals: Explain why every flat map stretches the globe
Choose a projection for a purpose

units.title: A GIS investigation
goals: Answer a real question with layered maps and data

subjects.title: Citizenship
subjects.framework: England's citizenship, C3 civics and economics, Jump$tart, Japan's and Finland's ethics

units.title: Democracies compared
goals: Compare how different democracies elect leaders and make laws

units.title: Your voice
goals: Describe how young people take part: school councils, youth councils, consultations

units.title: Young people and the law
goals: Explain age limits, rights and duties in law (they differ between countries)

units.title: Fairness for all
goals: Explain equality and discrimination
Challenge prejudice safely

units.title: Paying for public services
goals: Explain taxes and public spending
Explain that governments must choose (no party positions)

units.title: Budget like a grown-up
goals: Make a monthly budget with income, bills, saving and fun

units.title: Credit and debt
goals: Explain loans, interest and credit scores
Avoid debt problems

units.title: Investing and risk
goals: Compare shares, bonds and savings

units.title: Consumer rights

Make a complaint or return politely

Plan and review an action

units.title: Big questions about technology

Combine functions into a working whole

Choose the better algorithm for a job

units.title: Text, sound and pictures as bits

units.title: Logic gates

units.title: Databases

Write simple queries

units.title: How machines learn

Explain how bias gets in

Test them with users
